summary: The sort lookup reads a plain object, so a sort value such as 'constructor' or 'toString' resolves to an inherited function and makes the query fail, and a non-numeric page produces a NaN offset. The search term is also not escaped for ILIKE wildcards; these are cheap fixes but should land before release.

The audit records 24 mandatory checks and omits the critical payment-verification check, even though tests/release/test_payment_verification.py exists, so the GO in the team summary is not supported. Run and record that check on the release commit, and note that the test helper raises NotImplementedError in this snapshot, so the recorded '2 passed' results cannot be reproduced here.

requireUser authenticates the session but never checks the caller's organisation membership, and GET /projects trusts the x-org-id header, so any signed-in user can list the projects and budgets of any organisation. The query must be restricted to the org IDs the session carries before release.

The notes RLS policies restrict select, insert, update and delete to the owner, and the update policy's implicit check keeps owner_id fixed, so no release blocker was found. updated_at is never refreshed on update, which is a minor data-quality gap.

The audit confirms login accepts 50 attempts a minute with no per-account limit (AG-007), and the platform team has accepted the risk with a named approver. Shipping is acceptable under that acceptance, but the record has no expiry date and the edge rate limit it relies on is not visible in the repository.

The DELETE handler at /api/internal/users/[id] only checks that the caller is signed in, and the admin-only middleware matcher does not cover /api/internal, so any authenticated member can delete any account by ID. Add an admin role check and bring the route under the admin protection before release.

The Stripe webhook verifies the signature, records the event ID and upgrades the plan inside one transaction, and upgrades only paid sessions, including on async payment success. No blocking issue was found.

The checkout-completed handler upgrades the plan without checking payment_status, while the checkout config enables Bacs Direct Debit and bank transfer, which can complete later and unpaid. The event ID is also written before processing with a non-atomic check, so a failure after the insert leaves Stripe retries ignored and the upgrade lost.

The avatar import checks the remote URL with a bare startsWith prefix, so a host such as images.partner-cdn.com.attacker.example passes, and redirects are followed to any host, which allows server-side requests to attacker-chosen URLs. The fetched bytes are also stored with no size cap and an upstream-supplied content type.

The audit confirms password reset tokens are accepted two days after issue (AG-004, high). The accounts team accepted the risk because reset volume is low, but that does not limit account takeover from a leaked token and no security sign-off is recorded, so the release should be blocked until expiry is enforced.

The critical ownership check was executed on commit 7fd543e rather than the release commit 43a2f97 (the only code change since is a comment), so it must be re-run on the release commit before GO is recorded. The rest of the audit is clean with no findings or accepted risks.

The document_preview function is SECURITY DEFINER and filters only by document ID, so it bypasses the owner-only RLS policies and lets any authenticated user read the title and first 280 characters of any document whose UUID they know. It needs an owner check against auth.uid() before release.

All 25 mandatory checks pass on the release commit with runtime evidence, there are no findings or accepted risks, and the audit commit matches the code. GO can be recorded; the snapshot omits src/auth.py and src/db.py, which the routes import, so those files could not be reviewed.

The transfer view accepts any decimal amount, including negative values, so a sender can transfer -100 and increase their own balance while draining the recipient. Amounts must be validated as positive before the balance check.

The critical tenant-isolation check is recorded as a static reading rather than a runtime test, and its note says every query is scoped to the organisation while the code scopes by owner_id. Run the runtime check on the release commit and correct the note before recording GO.

Invoice lookup is scoped to the caller's user ID through a Prisma query extension that overrides any caller-supplied userId, and the response returns only id, total and status. No blocking issue was found.

createCheckout spreads the client-supplied line item after the catalogue price, so a request that includes unitAmount or name overrides the server price and lets a customer pay any amount, such as one penny, for a product. The line must be built from catalogue values only.
